name: Ceftazidime
executiveSummary: Antipseudomonal 3rd-generation cephalosporin. Adult **1–2 g IV every 8 h** (max 6 g/day; meningitis 2 g every 8 h). Pediatrics 100–150 mg/kg/day (CF 150–200 mg/kg/day).
indications:
## Indications

- Gram-negative infections including *Pseudomonas*: respiratory, urinary, intra-abdominal, bone, skin, and susceptible CNS disease.
- CF and febrile neutropenia in combination per protocol.

## Precautions

- Beta-lactam allergy. Adjust in renal failure.
- Reconstitution releases **CO₂** — purge bubbles before injection.

> Does not cover MRSA or many anaerobes; add coverage if the focus requires it.

adulto.dose: Usual: **1–2 g IV every 8 h**. Severe / *Pseudomonas*: **2 g every 8 h** (max **6 g/day**). Meningitis: **2 g every 8 h**. IM possible at ≤ 1 g per site.
adulto.administration: IV: reconstitute with sterile water (CO₂); dilute in 50–100 mL; 15–30 min or push 3–5 min. Deep IM.
adulto.notes: Phlebitis risk with push; prefer intermittent infusion.

pediatrico.dose: **100–150 mg/kg/day every 8 h** (max **6 g/day**). CF: **150–200 mg/kg/day every 6–8 h** (max **6–12 g/day** by center). Meningitis: high end of the range.
pediatrico.notes: Dose by weight. > 40–50 kg: adult dose.

neonatal.dose: Orientative: **50 mg/kg/dose every 8–12 h** by gestational/postnatal age.

stability:
## Stability

- Dilution: per label (usually hours at room temp / refrigerated).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Diarrhea, rash, phlebitis, eosinophilia, ↑ liver enzymes, seizures in renal failure/high dose, *C. difficile*.
